category_title: Disruptive students who feel targeted and disrespected by authority figures
minimal_context: Kyle is explaining his side of the story regarding a classroom incident during a Youth Court hearing preparation.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Kyle, we need to go over your case. Please explain your side of the story about what happened in class.

STUDENT: I was just being loud because of what was going on. I made a remark, and the teacher warned me and put my name on the board.

TUTOR: Okay. And what about your relationship with the dean of discipline, Mrs. W?

STUDENT: I do not get along with her. She makes fun of me by calling me by my wrong last name.

TUTOR: Let's stay on track. People mispronounce names sometimes, so let's just focus on the facts.

STUDENT: No, she is intentionally mispronouncing my last name to disrespect me! She has frequent contact with me and still says it wrong on purpose. You guys aren't even listening to my side!

options.A: Joke a lot and laugh at oneself during the case preparation with the student.
options.B: Use repetition and expansion to explore and define the student's feelings about the incident.
options.C: Ask why in a caring manner, such as asking why he made the remark.
options.D: Listen without interruption and permit all possible perspectives to emerge regarding the incident.
